nonPoolDecisions: Reading (2012: Léamhthuiscint A and B both compulsory): every printed question is a whole card and each printed part, (a) and (b), a practice card at its published tariff. 2012 prints (b) as one part asking two questions with no (i)/(ii); the scheme marks them separately as (b)(1) and (b)(2), 2 marks each (PDF 16), so they are two criteria of the (b) card and of the whole card, not two cards.

Single-answer parts allow only the mark values the scheme prints for them (0, the printed prices and partials, and the full tariff): the third-person deductions (B 1(a) 3-1, 1(b)(2) and 4(b)(2) 2-1), A 1(a)’s “=(3-1)=2m” and “= (3-1 marc)”, A 3(a)’s “=(3-1) iomarcach”, B 5(a)’s “(3-1m),freagra easnamhach”, B 5(b)(2)’s “(2-1m)”, A 3(b)(2)’s two ways at 1 each, and B 3(b)(1) and 4(b)(1)’s answers naming two things at 1 + 1.

A 6(b) is one 12-mark answer: the scheme marks an answer naming only one view out of 8 and a bare retelling out of 7, and prints no split; it is one criterion. B 6(b) is the genre 2 and two traits with an example each, 5 + 5 (“T1 + S1 (5m) = T2+ S2 (5m) =”), three criteria of one card.

Prose: 2A (Hurlamaboc) and 2B (an optional novel extract) are a card each; poetry 3A (An tEarrach Thiar) and 3B (an optional modern poem) a card each with their three printed sub-questions as criteria; Ceist 4A–4F a card each, 4F’s three sub-questions as criteria. Every literature card carries one shared 5-mark Gaeilge award.
caveats: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 Léamhthuiscint A 50 + B 50 (Ceist 1–5 at 7: (a) 3, (b) 2 + 2; Ceist 6 at 15: (a) 3, (b) 12); Ceist 2 Prós 30 (Eolas 25 + Gaeilge 5); Ceist 3 Filíocht 30 (Eolas 14 + 4 + 7 + Gaeilge 5); Ceist 4 Litríocht Bhreise 40 (Eolas 35 + Gaeilge 5).

The reading key prints its prices in a short unit wherever a line ends (“=3m.”, “”3m”, “”2m”, “= 0 m.”, “=(3-1)=2m.”, “= (3-1 marc)”, “S1= 1m”, “”1+1m”, “T1 + S1 (5m) =”) and a tariff only on A 3(a), A 5(b)(2), B 2(b)(2), B 3(b)(1), B 6(a) and B 6(b); the section rule on PDF 16 prices every other part. Accepted answers are quotations from the passage, some numbered “(1) … (2) …”.

The literature scheme prints nothing but each question reprinted with its Eolas tariff: 2A and 2B (Eolas 25, from the NB “Sa Phrós mar sin 25 ar Eolas” and the note “Caithfidh an Scrúdaitheoir an marc as 25 (Ábhar) agus as 5 (Gaeilge) a thaispeáint”, printed once after both); 3A and 3B “(14 marc)”, “(4 marc)”, “(7 marc)” where the paper prints 14, 6 and 10; 4A–4E “(35 marc)”; 4F (i) “(3 marc)” + “(16 marc)”, (ii) “(8 marc)”, (iii) “(8 marc)”.

Grade table: PDF 26 prints “Grádú Marcála sna Ceisteanna” (grades A–D for totals 200 to 5) on its own page after Ceist 4, naming no question; note 3 on PDF 25, in the numbered notes for Ceisteanna 2–4, advises examiners to think in grades and use “an réríomhaire (cf lch 25)” when deciding what an answer is worth (the table is on printed page 24; printed page 25, PDF 27, is blank). It is carried as printed and never read for rows.

Dá bhféadfainn, dhéanfainn rud daoibh
Nár dheineas riamh dom féin -
Mhaithfinn daoibh gach peaca
’s d’agróinn cogadh ar phéin! (10 marc)
(iii) Cén mothú is mó a mhúscail dearcadh na máthar ionat féin? (Is leor dhá phointe eolais.) (10 marc)
